title: POC weekly - latency tuning (TTFT, streaming, sequence length)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review TTFT results, streaming behavior, sequence length distribution, and kernel choices. Action items agreed: run streaming benchmarks, share TTFT spreadsheet, provide kernel config options, and provision sample peak traffic for next tests.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: okay everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, we'll kick off, we got Mei from SE and Liam in the background. Uh Sam, Priya, Marcus, thanks for being here
00:18 Sam: thanks, yeah morning, we ran the TTFT batch yesterday, got some odd numbers when streaming was enabled, so keen to walk through
00:36 Mei: cool, I pulled the run results, quick note, some names in the logs got mangled, the test used red wood ded- Redwood Dedicated model variant, quant8 configs, sequence lengths at 128 and 512, and streaming flag on for half the traffic
00:58 Priya: yeah we saw first token latencies spiking to ~180ms which surprised us, expected closer to 90ms from your demo last week
01:12 Mei: right uh so a couple things, TTFT for streaming has more moving parts, network + chunking + kernel warmup. We saw consistent ~85ms in non-streaming path for 128, but streaming with 128 chunked to 64 tokens added overhead so that explained some of the delta
01:36 Marcus: is that due to the chunk size or due to the kernel switch between streaming and non-streaming?
01:48 Mei: both - chunking causes more calls to the runtime and if the kernel path picks a different matmul kernel for short sequences you pay setup cost. Also, kv cache warmup for streaming is still not fully amortized on small prefixes, so first few requests look worse
02:12 Jordan: let me jump in, worth noting our runtime does continuous batching and sometimes when you enable streaming we avoid large batch windows to keep TTFT down, but that reduces batching gains so marginal token latency goes up
02:31 Sam: ok makes sense, what about sequence length distribution? Our production has 70% under 64 tokens, 25% 64-256, 5% >512.
02:45 Mei: that distribution is actually friendly for streaming because small sequences benefit from chunking and you get partial responses. But you need to tune chunk size to not create too many tiny RPCs. For your mix I'd recommend chunk 128 with internal chunking of 64 for long tails
03:08 Priya: and kernel choices? We saw the profiler picking a different kernel on T4 (we're testing on T4 infra) vs your internal A100 runs
03:20 Mei: yeah T4 has fewer fused kernels for attention and the matmul tiling differs; on A100 you get our optimized fp16/quant kernels, T4 may fall back to a generic path. I can share a table of kernel mappings we observed
03:36 Marcus: also, we saw some jitter when concurrent streams > 8, CPU went high on the node handling the chunking logic
03:48 Mei: right that was the chunk coordinator thread, we can pin chunking to different cores or increase worker threads; there's a tradeoff with CPU cost. For the POC we can test pinning and measure.
04:10 Sam: any quick wins? We're under time pressure to reduce TTFT for demo next Wednesday
04:18 Jordan: immediate wins: 1) reduce chunking overhead by increasing chunk size to 128 for your profile, 2) pre-warm KV cache with a synthetic prefix run before demo, 3) disable aggressive batching in controlled runs so first token path is stable. We'll send a checklist and scripts
04:38 Priya: can you confirm the pre-warm won't leak customer data?
04:44 Mei: yes it uses synthetic tokens and our KV warmup API marks data as ephemeral, SOC two controls applied, logs will show ephemeral indicator, I'll include the security note
05:02 Marcus: about kernel selection, can you force a kernel in the runtime for the POC to evaluate latency vs throughput?
05:12 Mei: we can force kernel selection per model version in the config. For T4 we can try the tiled matmul variant and also a quant fallback to see latency delta. I'll run both and share numbers
05:26 Sam: great. Also competitors - we did a quick comparison, Anthropic's streaming looked decent but their TTFT was similar, OpenAI had lower TTFT on small models but cost was higher, Vertex AI gave us worst jitter.
05:40 Jordan: thanks for that intel. We'll include competitive baseline in the spreadsheet.
05:48 Priya: action wise, timeline?
05:52 Jordan: Mei will run streaming tests with chunk sizes 64/128/256 and seq len 512 tails by Friday. I'll send TTFT spreadsheet today and a step-by-step to pre-warm. Priya will provision a 30-minute peak window next week for a live run.
06:14 Mei: quick note - logs show occasional "KV cash miss" typo in the agent log, that's just a transcription artifact but the event is a cold prefix miss
06:26 Sam: haha ok noted. Anything else on security or procurement?
06:30 Priya: we still need our security pack and KMS integration details, plus SSO flow for service accounts
06:36 Jordan: Lia from security sent the pack last week, but I'll re-share and add KMS/HSM notes. We'll confirm SSO flow and RBAC mapping.
06:48 Marcus: can you include the kernel config file and a short runbook for toggling streaming? Our ops team will want to automate tests
06:56 Mei: yes I'll attach the runtime snippets and CLI flags.
07:02 Jordan: ok let's do quick recap and next steps
07:08 Jordan: recap: Mei runs streaming latency matrix (chunk 64/128/256 x seq 128/512), force-kernel tests on T4, provide logs; Jordan sends TTFT spreadsheet + pre-warm script + security pack; Priya provisions peak window and shares access; Sam to confirm demo time; all by dates in action items.
07:28 Sam: sounds good thanks everyone
07:30 Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in calendar and slack, talk soon
07:34 [END TRANSCRIPT]
